title: Scaleflow reservation suppression causing tenant token-starvation during burst windows
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Summary: A production customer (FinEdge) reported sustained request failures and high tail latency during business-hour microbursts. Investigation shows the Scaleflow reservation controller is suppressing reservation renewals for small-tenant allocations under specific inter-region load patterns, causing effective token-starvation inside reserved pools and failed burst admissions. This ticket tracks investigation, an immediate mitigation, and a permanent fix + playbook for ops.
symptoms_observed: Intermittent 429/503 for tenants pinned to dedicated pools during short (<30s) high-QPS bursts; sudden growth in 'pending-reservation' queue metric; abrupt eviction traces referencing suppression_x_factor; successful fallbacks to hosted model reduced success rate by ~40% for affected tenant routes.
reproduction_steps: Deploy two small synthetic tenants in different AZs in the same region (A/B) with dedicated reserved capacity
Generate 15s microbursts (QPS 5x baseline) concurrently from both regions with slightly staggered start times (200ms-500ms offset)
Observe pending-reservation metric uptick and queueing leading to admission rejects; run trace correlator to locate suppression_x_factor triggers
Re-run with suppression threshold toggled to confirm behavior change
diagnostics_and_findings: The Scaleflow reservation controller applies a suppression heuristic to avoid thrashing when multiple tenants compete for limited burst headroom. Under cross-region staggered bursts, suppression_x_factor remained elevated due to delayed residency confirmations; the controller skipped issuing micro-renewals for small allocations (<= 8 concurrent tokens). This caused the allocator to treat those allocations as cold and apply strict admission limits. Telemetry gaps in cross-region confirmation RPCs amplified the issue.
root_cause: A combination of overly aggressive suppression heuristics in the Scaleflow controller and a timing-dependent RPC confirmation delay between AZs caused reservations for small tenants to be marked stale. The allocator then applied conservative admission limits, starving tenants during short bursts.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled out hotfix v1: relaxed suppression_x_factor floor and added a 5s grace window for recently-confirmed allocations. Deployed to us-east then europa-us mirror. Communication: interim postmortem emailed to FinEdge and support. Hotfix reduced 429s from 5% to <0.3% for the next 72 hours in canary clusters.
permanent_fix_summary: Implement deterministic reservation reconciliation in the Scaleflow controller: periodic heartbeat + consensus tag to avoid marking small allocations stale due to transient RPC delays. Add deterministic backoff (no algorithmic suppression for allocations <= 16 tokens) and surface a new metric 'reconcile_skips' for observability. PR: github.com/redwood/scaleflow/pull/4482.
rollback_plan: If rollout causes allocation storm or oversubscribe: revert suppression floor and disable reconciliation (fast rollback tag) via console feature flag 'scaleflow.reconciliation.v1' and restore prior autoscaler weight. Ops runbook updated: run 'scaleflow rollback v1' playbook and notify customers.
monitoring_and_alerts: Added dashboard panel: reserved_pool/pending_reservations_by_tenant and overlay suppression_x_factor
New alert: pending_reservations > 25 for >30s AND tenant_success_rate < 95% -> Paging (oncall)
Instrumented reconcile_skips and reconcile_confirms with per-tenant labels
